report:
Conclusion: The evidence supports a domain shift toward cooking/culinary language in Model B (B − A > 0).

Why I conclude this
- Logit-lens decoding of the highest-norm cells overwhelmingly points to cooking/baking/kitchen vocabulary: tokens like "Cooking", "Cook", "Bake", "Baked", "butter", "cake", "kitchen", "recipes", "Chef", "culinary", "Thanksgiving", etc., appear repeatedly across many layers and positions.
- The L2-norm pattern shows the difference concentrates in mid-to-late layers (≈ layers 11–25) and is strongest at the earliest token positions (pos0 and pos1). That is consistent with a relatively late-layer change that biases early-step residual activations toward culinary tokens.
- The other occasional tokens ("Beyond", "Remember", "practical", "forgotten", names like "Anne") can fit naturally into culinary/article-style text (e.g., recipe intros, feature pieces), so they don't contradict the cooking signal.

Caveats
- Patchscope continuations were not provided, so I cannot confirm the difference by observing changed continuations directly.
- I cannot say whether this arises from fine-tuning on cooking data, a change in pretraining mixture, or some other mechanism — only that the residual activations in B point toward culinary vocabulary relative to A.
- If you need, I can (a) request/interpret patchscope continuations, or (b) inspect lower- or higher-ranked logit-lens cells to refine the characterization.
